summary: El Alto International Airport (LPB) is one of the highest commercial airports in the world, sitting at approximately 4,061 meters (13,325 feet) above sea level on the Altiplano plateau above La Paz, Bolivia. It serves as the country's primary international gateway, handling the majority of Bolivia's international flights and connecting La Paz to destinations across the Americas and beyond. The airport's extreme altitude requires longer runways and special considerations for both aircraft performance and passenger health.
faqs:
Q: How high is El Alto International Airport?
A: The airport sits at approximately 4,061 meters (13,325 feet) above sea level, making it one of the highest international airports in the world.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown La Paz?
A: The airport is located in El Alto, roughly 8-10 km (5-6 miles) from La Paz's city center, but the drive can take 30-60 minutes depending on traffic and the winding descent down the canyon.

Q: Should I worry about altitude sickness when flying into LPB?
A: Yes, the high elevation can cause altitude sickness. It's advisable to stay hydrated, avoid alcohol upon arrival, rest for the first day, and consider consulting a doctor about altitude medication beforehand.

Q: Which airlines operate from El Alto International Airport?
A: Major carriers include Boliviana de Aviación (BOA), LATAM, Avianca, Copa Airlines, and Aerolineas Argentinas, with connections to cities throughout South America and some international destinations.
